crisis noun

also a crisis, in a crisis, critical moment, turning point, emergency, the situation is critical

classical

Caes. B.G. 6.38.2: in summō rem esse discrīmine (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Phil. 7.1
Traupman 186, 299

discrīmen, discrīminis n.

noun, third declension · Declension on Wiktionary

a crisis, a critical moment

Properly a dividing line or interval; then the point that decides between two outcomes, a turning point, a crisis, a danger. Its common everyday sense is a difference (sine discrīmine, without distinction).

Other words

  • angustiae, angustiārum f. pl. — difficulties, straits, a tight spot

    noun, first declension, plural · also used · classical · Caes. B.C. 1.54: cum in hīs angustiīs rēs esset (Lewis & Short); Cic. Quinct. 5: in summās angustiās addūcī · Declension on Wiktionary

    Properly a narrow place, a pass; then any tight spot, and shortage of money (angustiae reī familiāris).

  • tempus, temporis n. — a critical time, the circumstances

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Declension on Wiktionary

    Especially in the plural, the times, of hard or dangerous circumstances (Lewis & Short): amīcōrum temporibus, to a friend’s difficulties (Cic. Fam. 10.1.2).

Examples

  • Rēs est in summō discrīmine.

    The situation is critical.Traupman 186

See also risk, economic, problem.
